text:
Kirill Kaprizov has 37 points in 22 games, 17 goals (his OT winner against Montreal on Nov. 10 was the league-leading 17th, per WDAY Radio), and an 11-game point streak (6 goals, 14 assists) that has carried the Wild through a run of eight wins in ten. He plays 21:29 a night, and Minnesota takes 56.6% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five when he's out there.

Some of this will cool, and that's fine. He's shooting 24% against 17% last season, and the Wild have scored 7.9 more goals than expected with him on the ice. The chances themselves are real: 13.6 expected goals on his own shots is elite volume, and our range still has him finishing with about 111 points.

What to watch is how he gets there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 57% of his entries last season and setting up teammates at an 87th percentile rate. When the shots stop falling, the passing is what keeps the streak alive. Three assists in Toronto and two in Boston say it already is.
headline: Kaprizov is leading the league and the Wild are winning
